prereg.grid_rule: the smallest listed cell size whose bounding box fits max_cells is used; because the box is an upper bound on cells inside the study area, the cap can never be breached after the choice

sources: usgs_sciencebase (USGS data release: inundation polygons or high-water marks)
portal_download (open-data portal file, filtered to the event window)
petabencana_area (RW-level flooded areas, else buffered reports)
label.observable_rule: EMS: inside the activation AOI; S1/S2: observed in both periods; USGS: inside the product footprint

social.gdelt_text: title (from 2019-09-22) + URL slug + GKG location names; earlier events have no titles

geoparsing.added: v6 (applied to every city); amended in v6.1
geoparsing.gazetteer: GeoNames country extract (download.geonames.org/export/dump/<CC>.zip, CC BY 4.0), feature class P codes PPL, PPLX, PPLL, PPLF, PPLS, PPLA2-5 inside the study area (name, ASCII name and Latin-script alternate names); generic words, major places, names used > 2 km apart and names shared with towns outside the area removed. v5.5.1: replaces the OSM/Overpass gazetteer, which was unavailable for 7 of 9 cities in v5.5.0. v6: the GeoNames feature that IS the study city/region (any of its names equal to a self-name) is excluded with all its alternate names
geoparsing.outside_places: GeoNames populated places (population >= 1000, not sections) within outside_places_buffer_km of the study area but outside it
geoparsing.ner_geocoding: Nominatim, bounded to the study box, up to 5 candidates; accepted only if a settlement unit (suburb ... town) whose name equals the NER name, accents ignored; streets, POIs, rivers and administrative areas never accepted; v6: the query is the name alone (bounded box), not name + alias
geoparsing.dropped: month and weekday names; the study city's own names; major cities, regions, countries
geoparsing.diagnostic: effective number of mention locations (1/HHI) and top-place share, logged and written to provenance
geoparsing.self_names: names denoting the whole study area (city, region, storm, main river) are retrieval keywords only, never locations; v5 wrongly used the retrieval alias list here, which removed every within-area town listed as an alias from the social layer
geoparsing.toponym_rule: t5 = t4 plus one final filter. t4 = t3 applied to every name placed from text. a gazetteer match counts only if the text holds an occurrence that is either a GDELT-structured location placed in the study area ('<name>, <home region/country>') or a capitalised, complete name in prose (no adjacent feature word or name particle, no adjacent capitalised word outside title-case headlines, no qualifier placing it elsewhere, not a common word of the city's language or English at Zipf >= 4.5); names that are countries, continents or first-level divisions of the study country never count; lower-case occurrences (URL words) do not count on their own. v6.1 (t4): (1) names found by NER must pass this same rule before they are geocoded (under t3 only gazetteer names were tested, and NER re-admitted the names t3 had rejected); (2) flood and weather words of the study languages are never place names; (3) a NER name that is a gazetteer name keeps the gazetteer's coordinates. v6.1.1 (t5): a mention is kept only if its text holds an occurrence that passes the rule with the name as the WHOLE first component of a structured location ('Vargas, <home region>' counts; 'Getulio Vargas, <home region>' does not). Routing to NER is unchanged (t4); the filter only removes mentions
geoparsing.location_unit: mentions are counted on a ~250 m lattice (0.0025 deg) for every resolution path
geoparsing.version_note: g4 accepts exactly what g3 accepted (a settlement unit in the study box whose name equals the queried name). The version is new only so that v6.0's lookup caches, which could hold a failed or refused lookup as 'no such place', are not read: non-empty v6.0 answers are reused, empty ones are asked again
geoparsing.text_cleaning: v6.1: document text is entity-decoded (HTML entities, twice for RSS), stripped of tags and whitespace-normalised before any matching; v6.0 left GDELT's numeric entities in titles

social.query_terms: keyword APIs (news RSS, Reddit comments, YouTube) are queried with the event language's flood terms and English: es inundación/DANA/riada, it alluvione/allagamento/esondazione, pt enchente/inundação/alagamento, id banjir/genangan, en flood/flooding/waterlogging

geotagged_photos.sources: Flickr (flickr.photos.search, has_geo, API key) and Wikimedia Commons (geosearch; identified User-Agent, paced, Retry-After honoured; keyless). v6.1.1: a geosearch tile that returns the API maximum (500 files) is split into four and read again, down to ~140 m, so dense areas are read completely
geotagged_photos.rule: photo TAKEN inside the social window, inside the study box, with flood vocabulary in its title, tags, description or categories; Flickr location accuracy >= 12 (neighbourhood or finer)
geotagged_photos.dedupe: one photo per author, ~100 m spot and day
geotagged_photos.timeliness: photos may be uploaded after the event; they measure where flooding was photographed, not what was known in real time (stated as a limitation; a sensitivity analysis drops them)

social.deduplication: (1) syndicated wire copies: identical GDELT location list, tone vector and title count once; (2) identical text (160 normalised characters) counts once; (3) photos as above
social.acquisition_completeness: v6.1: a city's social layer is COMPLETE when every enabled source answered and every candidate place name was looked up. A source that fails (rate limit, timeout, server error) and a geocoder cap or failure leave the stage unfrozen, so the next run retries; failed lookups are never cached as 'not found'. Only complete acquisitions are analysed (an explicit override analyses incomplete ones as provisional and flags them)
social.signal_naming: v6.1: the layer is named after what it contains. Sources are classed as news (GDELT, news RSS), social media (Reddit, YouTube), geotagged photos (Flickr, Commons) and crowdsourced reports (PetaBencana); a layer is called by a kind only if that kind carries >= 80% of its located primary-window mentions, else 'mixed'

cv.tile_rule_text: tile = correlogram range (autocorrelation < 0.1) minus the buffer, rounded up to 500 m, within [tile_m, tile_max_m]; stepped down by 500 m while fewer than 3 x k tiles contain flooded cells (Roberts et al. 2017)

computation.checkpointing: every stage and every ladder rung is written to cache/ as soon as it finishes; a disconnected run resumes instead of restarting
computation.rung_reuse: rungs with identical feature sets are computed once and reused across orderings
computation.missing_data: coarse reanalysis gaps are filled from the nearest valid cell, never a city median
computation.per_city_grid: grid_m may be raised for a study area too large at 100 m; reported per city

inference.note: early fusion gets its own (smaller) toroidal null because each shift needs XGBoost refits

gated_grid.rule: (alpha, tau) chosen on training tiles by AP; alpha = 0 always admissible

robustness.added: v5.4.1, after the Chennai_2015 and Valencia_2024 runs; reported as robustness, never as primary
robustness.gradient_excluding_R0: primary gradients recomputed without R0 (no physical features); role robust_excl_R0
robustness.gated_wide_grid: most complete rung refitted with alphas 0..6 and taus 0 (= ungated) ..0.7; reports how often the gate is used, switched off, or replaced by ungated addition
robustness.fold_diagnostics: per-fold cells, positives and prevalence (fold_diagnostics.csv); flagged when the range exceeds 25 percentage points
robustness.learner_logistic: most complete rung refitted with a standardised logistic regression as the physical learner (all operators, nulls and bootstrap), so verdicts do not hinge on XGBoost
robustness.without_photos: top rung refitted without the geotagged photo sources (timeliness check)
robustness.stability_flag: v6.1: a sensitivity variant is flagged 'unstable' when it flips the sign of the top-rung stacked effect by more than the SESOI or moves it by more than 5 x SESOI

label_ai4g.note: AI4G detections inside the event window; a cell is flooded when detections cover >= 25% of it (20 m pixels assumed, per the dataset's Sentinel-1 input resolution)

analysis_plan.fixed: 29 Sep 2026, v6, before any v6 acquisition. Seen at that point: v5.5.2 localisation statistics (label-free) and v5.5.0 results for Chennai_2015 and the architecture effects. AMENDED 2 Oct 2026 (v6.1) AFTER the v6.0 run of ten cities had been analysed and reviewed: see 'v61_amendment'. The amendment changes no endpoint, test, SESOI or verdict rule. AMENDED again 3 Oct 2026 (v6.1.1): see 'v611_amendment'

research_questions.RQ1: At the most complete physical rung, does each fusion operator (legacy entropy-gated ADR, tuned gated, stacked late fusion, early fusion) change held-out AP? Pooled across cities by random-effects meta-analysis. Confirmatory set: every tier-A city.
research_questions.RQ2: Within a city, does the social layer's marginal value decline as physical completeness rises? Slope of the null-centred gain on held-out physical AP across the ordered ladder, tile-bootstrap CI, one-sided test.
research_questions.RQ3: Is the social layer's value general across cities, and what explains its variation? (a) random-effects meta-analysis of the per-city slopes and top-rung effects over every tier-A city; (b) pre-registered moderator: the social layer's localisation (log effective number of mention locations, label-free) in a mixed-effects meta-regression (REML, Knapp-Hartung, permutation p); (c) the localisable subset pooled as a conditional secondary analysis, whatever its size.

co_primary_endpoints: info_nats_fm_adj (cross-validated estimate of I(Y;S|R), the quantity the saturation definition is about)
secondary_endpoints: headroom-normalised gradients info_frac_fm_adj = I/H(Y|R) and dAPh_fm_adj = dAP/(1-AP)
all gradients without R0; ordering B
analysis_plan.primary_ordering: A_terrain_first (B_surface_first is a robustness check of ordering dependence)
analysis_plan.confirmatory_set: gt_tier == A_authoritative (all such cities, localisable or not). v5.5 restricted the confirmatory set to localisable cities; v6 keeps localisation as the moderator instead, so no city is excluded on a property of its social layer

localisation_eligibility.basis: label-free: computed from the located mentions in the primary window only (effective locations = 1/Herfindahl index of mention locations). Selecting on R0 information gain instead would bias the slope downward (regression to the mean at the first rung), so it is never used for selection.
localisation_eligibility.role: defines the conditional secondary set and the forest-plot marking only

analysis_plan.multiplicity: Holm across (tier-A cities) x (2 co-primary endpoints), ordering A, one-sided slope tests; headline tests: pooled RQ3 slope (confirmatory set) and the localisation moderator. v6.1: the confirmatory localisation moderator is tested on 7 outcomes (2 gradient slopes, 5 top-rung effects); Holm across those 7 on the reported p-value
analysis_plan.meta_analysis: REML tau^2 (fixed-point), Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman CI with max(1,q) truncation (k < 10), I^2, 95% prediction interval (k >= 3); per-city SE = tile-bootstrap SD of the slope
analysis_plan.sesoi_rationale: 0.01 AP: below the between-fold AP sd of every physical model in the v5.3-v5.4 runs and below operational relevance for ranking cells; 0.02 of the physical model's remaining held-out uncertainty for information
analysis_plan.equivalence: 'saturated' only if the 90% tile-bootstrap interval of the null-centred effect lies inside +/- SESOI (TOST at 5%); 'informative' needs the 95% interval above 0 and p_null <= 0.05; 'harmful' needs the 95% interval below 0; otherwise 'inconclusive'. v6.1 (reporting only): each effect also carries within_sesoi (the TOST result on its own) and a reading, so a non-zero effect whose 90% interval lies inside the SESOI is reported as negligible, not as informative; verdicts are unchanged
analysis_plan.density_placebo_design: GHSL GHS-POP (epoch nearest the event; WorldPop fallback) smoothed with the social kernel and transform replaces the social layer through the full ordering-A ladder (same folds, nulls, bootstrap; no early fusion). A decline that a pure population layer also shows is not evidence about event information. Control: the real social layer's gain at the top rung with population added to the physical model.
analysis_plan.blocking_check: label correlogram per city; the distance at which autocorrelation drops below 0.1 is compared with tile + buffer (2.5 km) and reported
analysis_plan.exploratory: meta-regression on physical lift and log mentions (descriptive)

moderator.name: log_effective_locations
moderator.test: two-sided; permutation p reported and used for k < 10
moderator.expectation: none pre-specified in sign for slopes; positive for top-rung gains

v61_amendment.seen_before_amending: all v6.0 results for the ten study cities (T1-T10), their run log and Porto Alegre's documents
v61_amendment.why: the v6.0 review found defects in the social layer (NER fallback bypassing the toponym rule; geocoder cap and failed sources frozen in checkpoints; HTML entities left in titles) and reporting gaps (pooled estimates carried by two cities; moderator tests uncorrected; two cities with 2 and 5 mentions)
v61_amendment.label_free: every changed rule acts on documents, place names, source handling or reporting; none uses a flood label or a model result as input
v61_amendment.status: a deviation from the v6.0 pre-registration (5e163339); results under v6.1 must be reported as obtained after this amendment

analysis_plan.study_set_note: v6.1: the study is these ten city-events (nine tier A, one tier B). NewYork_2021 (tier A, acquired under v6.0 but never analysed) and Bengaluru_2024 (tier C, acquired, never analysed) are left out by the author's decision of 2 Oct 2026, taken without any result for either city; Chennai_2023 has no usable label. Dropping a tier-A city from the v6.0 confirmatory set is a deviation. Only study-set cities are pooled

sensitivity_sets.evaluable: tier-A cities with >= 10 located mentions in the primary window (label-free; 10 is the existing min_source_mentions and sparse-layer threshold). Added in v6.1 after seeing that Carlisle (2) and York (5) have no usable social layer: a SENSITIVITY set. The confirmatory set is unchanged
sensitivity_sets.role: every pooled estimate and the moderator tests are repeated on it and reported beside the confirmatory ones

analysis_plan.influence: v6.1: for every pooled confirmatory estimate, each city's share of the random-effects weight and the leave-one-out estimate (T11); for the moderator, the leave-one-out range of the slope

v611_amendment.seen_before_amending: the v6.1 ACQUISITION of the ten cities (documents, located mentions, run log). No v6.1 analysis had been run: no label-based result existed under v6.1
v611_amendment.why: (1) Wikimedia Commons returned at most 500 files per ~9 km tile, so dense tiles (two of York's four) were truncated and their photos never examined; (2) a gazetteer name matched the END of a longer GDELT location ('Getulio Vargas, Rio Grande Do Sul' -> 'Vargas'): 8 of Porto Alegre's 80 primary mentions, 0-0.8% in the other nine cities
v611_amendment.label_free: both changes act on documents and place names only
v611_amendment.status: a deviation from the v6.1 pre-registration (4a03528b)

reporting.primary: per-fold metrics (mean over the 5 spatial folds), null-centred: the reported effect is the observed value minus the mean of the toroidal-null replicates
reporting.secondary: pooled out-of-fold metrics and the headroom-normalised dAPh_stacked, reported for continuity; the headroom denominator (1-AP) shrinks along the ladder and amplifies late rungs
reporting.why_null_centred: a toroidal-shifted social layer carries no flood information yet still moves AP a little (an extra smooth channel helps the learner), so raw deltas overstate the real gain
reporting.completeness: all cities, rungs, orderings, channels, sensitivity variants and the localisation audit (T9) are reported, including null results; v6.1: plus the influence table (T11), the acquisition status and the signal type of every city

tiers.A_authoritative: official event extent (CEMS, USGS data release, EA surveyed outline, NRSC)
tiers.A_authoritative_points: official point observations (USGS high-water marks, municipal points); sparse
tiers.B_crowdsourced: crowdsourced reports/maps; not independent of a social layer
tiers.C_satellite: satellite-derived reference (Sentinel-1/2 change, AI4G, GFD); not independent truth

ground_truth.event_specificity: Copernicus EMS products are kept only if their satellite image was acquired inside the label event window; ArcGIS extent layers only if their date is inside it; EA outlines are selected by their record id
ground_truth.unmapped_cells: cells outside a product's mapped area (EMS area of interest, USGS mapped-area boundary, depth-raster footprint, AI4G exclusion layer) are excluded as unknown, never scored as dry
circularity: a Sentinel-1-derived label (s1_change, ai4g_sar) removes the Sentinel-1 rung from every ladder
a PetaBencana label removes PetaBencana from the social layer
ground_truth.frozen_files: each city's vector ground truth is downloaded once and stored as one canonical GeoPackage (WGS84; layers 'labels' and 'coverage') with a SHA-256 manifest; runs read that file, so labels cannot change silently between runs
ground_truth.verification: every documented source URL is checked before the run and written to label_sources_status.csv
